result:
mitmweb now inserts live `flows/add` flows at the front when `view_order_reversed` is set and no column sort is active. I haven't run `npm test`, tsc, eslint or jest, so none of this has been executed.

**Changes**
- **`web/src/js/ducks/flows/index.ts`**:
  - `FlowsState` has a new `viewOrderReversed` field, defaulting to `false`. The reducer updates it from `OPTIONS_RECEIVE` and `OPTIONS_UPDATE`.
  - It is carried through the explicit state objects returned by the add, update and remove cases.
  - `FLOWS_ADD` inserts at position 0 when there is no sort column and the option is set. Otherwise it uses the existing sorted insert, so an active column sort still wins.
- **`web/src/js/ducks/flows/_utils.ts`**: new `insertViewItemAt(view, index, item, pos)` helper. `insertViewItem` now finds its position and calls it.
- **`web/src/js/__tests__/ducks/flows/indexSpec.tsx`**: new `view_order_reversed` tests:
  - The option is read from `OPTIONS_RECEIVE` and `OPTIONS_UPDATE`.
  - New flows go to the front when reversed and to the back when not.
  - An active column sort takes precedence over the option.

**Why a helper**
The no-sort comparator always returns 0, so `findInsertPos` always picks the end of the list. No constant comparator can make it pick the front, which is why I added the fixed-position insert.

**Left as-is**
As the task specified, the order restored when a column sort is toggled off is unchanged, so it may not follow the option. `FLOWS_UPDATE` for a flow not yet in the view (the WebSocket/HTTP race case) also still appends.

`flows/index.ts` now imports the option actions from `../options`. I didn't check whether that creates a circular import. If jest or tsc complains, that import is the first place to look.
